Meta.title: Causius — understand and answer legal letters
Meta.description: Causius reads an official letter with you: what it says, what it asks for and by when. When you need a person, it hands the case to a legal assistant or a licensed lawyer.

Footer.tagline: The legal layer of the fleet: an agent that does the legal work, and a person who decides.
Footer.disclaimer: Beta: running, not released. Causius gives legal information, not legal advice. Only a lawyer admitted where your matter is may advise you on it or represent you.
Footer.openSource: Open source under the MIT licence. Built in Zürich.

Home.tiersTitle: Three kinds of help, and an honest line between them
Home.tiersLead: Most legal trouble starts as paperwork, and most paperwork does not need a lawyer. Some of it does. Causius keeps the difference visible.

ai.name: Causius AI
ai.can: Reads, translates, lists what is asked and drafts a reply.
ai.limit: Legal information only. It does not advise or represent you.

assistant.name: Legal assistants
assistant.can: People who know the paperwork: gathering evidence, forms, filing, translation. They may work under a pseudonym.
assistant.limit: Not lawyers. They help you do it; they do not give legal advice.

lawyer.name: Licensed lawyers
lawyer.can: Admitted to practise where your case is; their admission is verified. They advise and can represent you, and may appear under a pseudonym until you engage them.
lawyer.limit: Licensed per jurisdiction: a lawyer in one country cannot advise on another's law.

Home.marketplaceLink: How the marketplace works, and how to join it

hero.kicker: Legal work, with you in charge
hero.lede: Causius is an AI legal workspace. Say what is happening or bring the letter: it finds what applies and cites it, keeps your deadlines, drafts what needs writing, and asks you before anything leaves your hands.

how.title: You decide. It does the work.

describe.title: Say what is going on
describe.body: In your own words, in English, German or French. Add the letter, the contract or any document; only its text is kept, encrypted.

work.title: Causius works the matter
work.body: It finds the rules that apply and cites them, computes and records the deadlines, and drafts the objection, the reply or the contract, ready to use.

approve.title: Nothing leaves without you
approve.body: Sending, filing, signing, sharing and paying are proposals you approve or decline. Where the law reserves a step for a lawyer, it says so.

privacy.title: Built so that nobody reads your matter

redact.title: Anonymised before any model
redact.body: Names, addresses, numbers and any words you add become placeholders before a model is asked anything, and are put back only on our server or in your browser.

sealed.title: Sealed at rest
sealed.body: Every matter has its own key. Titles, messages, deadlines and documents are stored encrypted; the database on its own names nobody.

pseudonymous.title: Pseudonymous on every side
pseudonymous.body: Clients, legal assistants and lawyers can all work under a pseudonym. A lawyer's admission is checked privately and their name disclosed to a client on engagement.

capabilities.title: What it does, and what comes next
capabilities.lede: Each line says whether it works today. The roadmap is public, and so is the record of what shipped.

fleet.title: The legal layer of a larger system
fleet.lede: Your OrangeCat account signs you in here, and the same account opens OrangeCat, Solon and Loki. Each does one job; together they let one person do what used to take a firm, a bank and a registry.

Helpers.metaDescription: The Causius marketplace: legal assistants who help with paperwork, and licensed lawyers who can advise and represent you.
Helpers.title: People who help when the AI is not enough
Helpers.lead: Two kinds of people work on Causius cases. What separates them is not price or rank but what the law lets each of them do. Neither needs to know who you are, and you need not know who they are until you engage one.
Helpers.noneBody: Causius does not match or verify anyone yet. Until it does, use the case file with a lawyer or advice centre you find yourself: it is made to be handed over.

assistant.name: Legal assistant
assistant.does1: Explains procedure and what an office usually expects
assistant.does3: Fills in forms with you, translates, prepares the filing
assistant.doesNot: Does not give legal advice, take a position on your case, or represent you.
assistant.checks: Planned: reputation earned on completed cases, confirmed by the person who was helped. A pseudonym keeps its history, so it cannot be shed.

lawyer.name: Licensed lawyer
lawyer.identity: Name or pseudonym; admission verified privately
lawyer.does1: Advises you on your rights and your options
lawyer.does2: Reviews or writes what you send
lawyer.does3: Represents you before the authority or the court
lawyer.doesNot: Only for the jurisdictions they are admitted in, shown on their profile.
lawyer.checks: Planned: admission checked privately against the public bar register of each jurisdiction before a profile carries this label, and re-checked. A lawyer may appear under a pseudonym; you learn their name when you engage them, because the law ties a lawyer's duties to their name.

Helpers.wantBody: Helpers are not Causius accounts. You offer your help as a service on OrangeCat, under your name or a pseudonym, and are paid there directly by the person you helped. You can list a service today. Causius does not yet pull those listings in, label them or check a lawyer's admission; that is the next thing on the roadmap.

label.title: The label is the law
label.body: Who may give legal advice is set by each country, and almost everywhere it is reserved to admitted lawyers. A helper's label says which side of that line they are on, and they may not work past it.

pseudonym.title: Pseudonymous on every side
pseudonym.body: People seeking help, legal assistants and lawyers can all appear under a pseudonym. Causius checks privately what has to be true — that a lawyer is admitted — and shows only what is needed. Many people who know a system best learned it by going through it, and would rather not put their name to that.

share.title: You choose what a helper sees
share.body: A helper gets the case file you hand them and nothing else, and by default that file is anonymised: the case, the deadline and the letter, with your name, address and numbers replaced. You decide if and when to tell them more.

place.title: Any jurisdiction, one at a time
place.body: A case names where it is. Helpers are matched on that place, the area of law and a language you share.

Settings.metaDescription: Use your own AI model for Causius analyses.
Settings.title: Settings
Settings.p1: Without a key, Causius reads letters with free shared models. They have a small daily budget that every visitor draws on, and they are not the strongest available.
Settings.p2: A legal letter deserves the best reading you can give it. Connect an API key from a provider below and your analyses run on the strongest model that key can use, on your own budget. The key is kept in this browser only: it is sent with each analysis to reach your provider and is never stored by Causius.
Settings.p3: Use an API key, ideally one with a spending cap. Causius never asks for a subscription login such as Claude Pro or ChatGPT Plus.

letters.name: Read an official letter
letters.body: Paste it or photograph it: what it says, what it asks of you, the deadline with the sentence it comes from, a translation and a draft reply. No account; names are removed in your browser first.

matters.name: Work a matter with an agent
matters.body: One workspace per matter: the conversation, research with numbered sources, deadlines, tasks, drafts and documents, behind your account.

approvals.name: Nothing leaves without your approval
approvals.body: Sending, filing, signing, sharing and paying are proposals that wait for your decision, recorded in the matter.

models.name: Any model, including your own
models.body: Free shared models by default, or your own key with one of ten providers, among them OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Mistral. The key stays in your browser.

domains.name: Check a name before you found on it
domains.body: The agent asks the domain registries themselves whether a name is registered, for any top-level domain, before it recommends one.

marketplace.name: Legal assistants and lawyers
marketplace.body: A marketplace where admitted lawyers and pseudonymous legal assistants offer their work, compete on price and quality, and are paid through OrangeCat.

formation.name: Found and register

contracts.name: Contracts that keep themselves
contracts.body: Agreements drafted here and signed by the parties, with every obligation tracked and, where the parties choose, payment held in escrow until it is met.

law.name: Law as data, from Solon
law.body: Statutes, procedures and jurisdictions as versioned, citable data, so every answer points at the exact rule it applied.

firms.name: Firms on their own models
firms.body: Law firms run Causius with models inside their own walls, so client data never leaves the firm.

Platform.metaDescription: The architecture of Causius: an agent that does legal work on a sealed case file, with every personal detail hidden from the models it uses.
Platform.title: How Causius is built, and why
Platform.lede: Legal help is expensive because legal work is slow, and it is slow because it is done by hand. Causius is an agent that does the work and a person who decides, built so that what it handles stays private and what it claims can be checked.

why.title: Why build it
why.p1: Most legal trouble never sees a courtroom. It is a letter with a deadline, a form, an objection, a contract, a registration: work with clear rules that is billed by the hour because nobody automated it.
why.p2: Language models can now do much of that work, but a chat window is the wrong shape for it. It forgets the deadline, keeps no file, and sends everything you type to whoever runs the model.
why.p3: So Causius is shaped like a case file with an agent attached, not like a chat. Lawyers stay where the law puts them; everything else gets done.

intake.title: Intake, in your browser
intake.body: The quick check reads letters and photos on your own device. Names, addresses and numbers are swapped for placeholders before anything is sent, and photos can be blacked out by hand first.

matter.title: The matter
matter.body: One record per matter: conversation, facts, deadlines, tasks, decisions and documents. One schema, shared by the analysis, the store and the export, and sealed with a key of its own.

agent.title: The agent
agent.body: A loop of tools: search and read the web for sources, record deadlines, tasks and facts, draft documents, check domain names, ask for approval. It may change the matter freely; anything that acts on the world it can only propose.

models.title: Models
models.body: Model-agnostic through the fleet's model kit: a chain of free models with health tracking, or your own key with one of ten providers. No vendor SDK and no pinned model, so a better model is a setting, not a rewrite.

identity.title: Identity and money
identity.body: Sign-in is OrangeCat, over OpenID Connect with PKCE. Causius keeps no users table and no password, only an account id. Paying helpers, with escrow, will run on OrangeCat too.

turn.title: One turn, start to finish
turn.lede: What happens between your message and the answer.
turn.s1: You write, or add a document. Only its text is kept, sealed.
turn.s2: The matter is opened with its own key and assembled: facts, open deadlines, decisions waiting, documents.
turn.s3: Every personal detail in it becomes a placeholder. The model reads [NAME-1], never the name.
turn.s4: The model works with tools for up to six rounds: searching, reading, recording deadlines, drafting. Arguments are restored on the server just before a tool runs.
turn.s5: Anything that would leave the matter becomes a proposal that waits for you.
turn.s6: The answer is restored, its sources numbered, and the turn sealed into the matter.

human.title: A person approves what matters
human.body: The agent does the work; a person decides what leaves. That one rule is what makes it safe to let it do everything else.

honest.title: Nothing claimed that is not true
honest.body: No invented statute, deadline, helper, rating or testimonial. Causius gives legal information, not advice: who may advise is set by law, not by us.

open.title: Open source
open.body: Every line is public under the MIT licence. Anyone can read how a letter is handled, check the claims on this site against the code, and run it themselves.

shared.title: Built from shared parts
shared.body: Design, sign-in, chat, models, rate limits and the public record come from packages the whole fleet uses, so a fix made once reaches every product.

stack.title: The stack
stack.lede: Boring where it can be, shared wherever two products need the same thing.

models.label: Models
models.value: @bitbaum/ai-kit · free chain · own keys · web search

tests.label: Tests
tests.value: Vitest · PGlite, a real PostgreSQL in process

next.title: From letters to legal existence
next.lede: Causius holds legal work: matters, founding and registering, and keeping contracts. The law itself (statutes, jurisdictions, procedures) belongs in Solon, as data every product can cite. Next comes the marketplace of lawyers and legal assistants, paid through OrangeCat.

Security.metaDescription: How Causius keeps legal matters private: anonymisation before any model, per-matter encryption at rest, a locked-down browser and approvals only the owner can give.
Security.title: Private by construction
Security.lede: Causius handles legal letters: names, addresses, residence, money. Each guarantee below is a property of the code, which is public. None of them asks you to trust us.

anon.title: Models are not told who
anon.body: Before any text goes to a model, personal details are replaced with placeholders, and they are put back only after the answer returns. Automatic detection is good, not perfect: check what is hidden before you send.
anon.d1: Found automatically: names in salutations and address blocks, street addresses, postcodes, email addresses, phone numbers, IBANs, AHV numbers, references and dates of birth.
anon.d2: Your own words to hide are always added, and so is the name on your account.
anon.d3: In the quick check this happens in your browser, before the letter leaves your device.
anon.d4: What the agent searches for on the web goes out with the placeholders too: a search engine never sees the name.
anon.d5: The one exception is your voice. If you speak instead of typing, the recording goes to a speech service to be turned into text, and a voice cannot be hidden first. It is not stored by Causius, you can edit the text before sending, and typing never involves it.

sealed.title: Sealed at rest
sealed.body: Each matter has its own data key, itself sealed by a master key that is never stored in the database.
sealed.d1: AES-256-GCM, a fresh nonce for every value, each bound to its matter and its purpose so it cannot be moved to another.
sealed.d2: Titles, messages, facts, deadlines, decisions and document text are all sealed. Only what sorting and routing need is in the clear: dates, statuses, the jurisdiction code, sizes.
sealed.d3: Without the master key, a copy of the database is noise.

minimal.title: Nothing kept that is not needed
minimal.body: An upload is reduced to its text and the file itself is dropped. A letter checked without an account is not stored at all.
minimal.d1: No users table and no passwords: sign-in is OrangeCat's, and Causius keeps only an account id.
minimal.d2: Logs record which model served a turn, never what was said. No analytics. The one extra script is the optional feedback widget, and it sends only what you write into it.

browser.title: A locked-down browser
browser.body: Every page is served with a strict content security policy.
browser.d1: Scripts run only with a nonce made for that one request, and a page may talk to Causius and nothing else.
browser.d2: No framing, no referrer, HSTS, and an isolated origin.
browser.d3: Answers from the API are never cached.

access.title: Only you decide
access.body: A matter opens only for the people in it. Anyone else gets the same answer as for a matter that does not exist.
access.d1: Actions that leave the matter are proposals only its owner can approve, and a decision is final.
access.d2: Limits per account keep the shared models from being drained.
access.d3: Deleting a matter deletes all of it: messages, deadlines, decisions and documents.

breach.title: If it went wrong
breach.lede: What each party would hold if the worst happened to it.

database.title: A stolen database
database.body: Ciphertext, account ids and dates. No names, no letters. Deadline dates are the one thing readable.

provider.title: A model provider's logs
provider.body: Placeholders where the people were: [NAME-1], living at [ADDRESS-1].

operator.title: Us, the operator
operator.body: We run the server that holds the master key, so we could be compelled. Keys that only you hold are on the roadmap; until then, that is the honest limit.

Ecosystem.metaDescription: Causius is the legal layer of a fleet of products — OrangeCat, Loki and Solon — that one OrangeCat account opens.
Ecosystem.title: One person, a whole fleet
Ecosystem.lede: Causius is one product in a fleet built to give a single person what used to take an institution. Each product does one job, and one OrangeCat account opens them all.
Ecosystem.unavailable: The list of products could not be loaded just now. Try again in a minute.
Ecosystem.layerBody: OrangeCat moves value, Loki gets the work done and Solon governs. Causius is the legal layer on top: the matters, registrations and contracts through which a person or an organisation exists in law and keeps its word. Solon holds the law as data; Causius does the legal work with it.

account.title: Sign in once
account.body: Your OrangeCat identity is your identity here, under a pseudonym if you like. Causius never sees your password.

pay.title: Pay and be paid
pay.body: Lawyers and legal assistants will be paid through OrangeCat, with the money held until the work is accepted.

build.title: Built and shipped by Loki
build.body: Loki's agents build Causius, and its deploy pipeline ships every change to this site.

law.title: The law, from Solon
law.body: Solon keeps rules as versioned data and decisions as signed votes. Causius will cite the law from it, rule by rule.

account.title: One account for all of it
account.body: Create it once at OrangeCat and use it for Causius, OrangeCat, Solon and Loki.
